newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR STARTS WEEK EASIER ON HARD UNITS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR STARTS WEEK EASIER ON HARD UNITS.

text.p: Trade on Zimbabwe's interbank foreign currency market resumed quietly on Monday after Thursday's break for the Independence holiday with the local dollar quoted easier on hard units, dealers said.
"The market is rather quiet but people are being cautious (and quoting high). They are trying to put feelers in the market to see if there's anyone who wants to sell," one dealer commented.
At 0735 GMT, the Zimbabwe dollar was trading softer on the U.S. dollar at 11.3000/3100 compared to 11.2975/3075 on Thursday.

Against the crosses it also weakened; to 18.4500/4700 from 18.3865/4130 versus sterling; to 6.6300/6400 against the mark from 6.5390/5480 and to 2.5400/5475 from 2.5290/5330 against South Africa's rand.
